Ample advice from many sources to avoid extra-cost extended warranties. I concur. However, I made an exception a couple years ago. Bought a battery-powered weed eater. A DeWalt. For the last year I have used it to mow the lawn. So many damn bumps and dips and gophers and tree roots the damn lawnmower was a pain-in-the-buttocks to push across the tops of the weeds. It was less effort to use the damn trimmer. To do the front and rear weed patches required starting with a full charge and doing two battery recharges. That was fine with me.

The DeWalt was well-built, solid and cut through weeds, vines and even small tree branches descending towards the ground. Whack. Severed.

A few days ago the charger was taking an inordinate amount of time to charge the battery. I unplugged the charger, removed the battery and a few minutes later put the battery into the charger and plugged it in and the on-board sensor began flashing in despair. The manual stated that there was a problem with either the battery or charger.

There was two days of manufacturer's warranty remaining. I discussed the affair with the Lowes folks where I bought the unit and the $40 extended replacement plan. We decided I should come back in two days when the replacement plan began (after manufactuerer's warranty expired) and make my claim then. I did that today. I was refunded the entire original purchase price including tax. The warranty plan cost was not refunded. Understandable.

Basically, I got two years of weed-eating usage for free. To simplify the refund process I agreed to having the refund placed on a Lowes gift card. I had done some basic research and wandered over to the trimmer aisle to get the cute sales' gal opinion (sweet Heather). She was a five-year veteran of the outside equipment area so had some good advice. The Sears Craftsman was not reliable. The Kroger is reliable but their trim line loading system received complaints from some folks. The GreenWorks had few returns and seemed reliable. It was also on sale. And I received a $15 price reduction for it being an open box. Contents indicated that the unit had not been assembled. Maybe someone opened the box to view the manual. Assured that if not satisfied to return the unit for replacement or refund. They had done that with the Kobalt trimmer I bought but was not satisfied with so returned for full refund. That was when I bought the DeWalt.

Cute Heather stated that battery-powered trimmers are continuously dropping in price. With sales tax the total cost of the GreenWorks trimmer was $146. The refund I received from the replacement warranty was $248. The new unit has some reviews and comments scattered across the Web and it looks promising that I will obtain good service from the unit.

The replacement warranty was altered a bit due to Lowes not selling DeWalt anymore. So a monetary refund was made. I needed a trimmer so I did not care that the Lowes card method was used. I need other shit Lowes sells so the card will soon be down to zero.

This was one instance where the extended warranty paid off. I did not go with the extended/replacement warranty with the new unit. Prices are dropping and it appears reliability is improving.

I will miss Mr. DeWalt. We decapitated a lot of weeds together. I am hoping there is a long happy life with Miss GreenWorks and I as we amble through the weeds together.
